title: Pilot weekly sync - capacity fencepost, fallbacks & request shaping
summary: Weekly pilot check-in focused on recent intermittent 5xxs and timeout cascades during batch billing runs. Root cause hypothesis: fencepost capacity allocations + tenant-level burst shaping causing queue reservoir starvation; agreed immediate mitigations include client-side shaping tweaks, temporary fallback routing to smaller model variant, and a benchmark run with controlled ramp to reproduce. Redwood to provide diagnostic script and sample autoscale/fallback config. Next sync after run and config applied.
next_steps: Redwood: share fencepost diagnostic script and sample autoscale + fallback policy (by 2026-10-09)
NimblePay: run controlled load with provided script and record p95/p99 (by 2026-10-12)
Diego: propose conservative client-side token-bucket defaults and sample retry header semantics (by 2026-10-08)
Schedule follow-up 30-min sync to review results (tentative 2026-10-13)
Elliot to confirm stakeholders for procurement if Dedicated needed (by 2026-10-20)
action_items: Maya Brooks | Redwood: attach link to sample fallback policy + autoscale snippet in email | due 2026-10-09
Diego Alvarez | Redwood SE: create and upload 'fencepost-check' repro harness (small python script) and instructions | due 2026-10-08
Priya Nair | NimblePay Eng: run harness during low-traffic window and save full traces, send logs to Redwood S3 share | due 2026-10-12
Samir Patel | NimblePay SRE: enable temporary increased span sampling to 50% for the pilot window and capture edge traces | due 2026-10-11
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we only have 45 minutes so let's go through the incident follow-up and the tuning plans. um, Diego's got the RCA sketch.
[00:12] Elliot Chen: Thanks Maya, yeah we saw those spikes on Saturday, about 15% of our batch billing jobs started to see 502/504s and then client retries piled up. Samir, do you want to summarize?
[00:24] Samir Patel: Sure, so top-level we saw two patterns: sharp 5xx bursts during the nightly billing window, and longer tail timeouts when clients retried aggressively. There's a kind of queue reservoir effect, once a tenant exceeded their burst tokens the requests were being queued, and then some were dropped.
[00:40] Priya Nair: We suspected rate limiting but it didn't line up with the tenant buckets, they were below their configured threshold. So something else was throttling downstream.
[00:49] Diego Alvarez: Right, preface: this is a bit of an off-by-one capacity allocation — the "fencepost" issue. When multiple workers scale at the same time the autoscaler pre-allocates N slots but the runtime's queueing layer assumes N-1 active slots for KV cache warmups, so a small percent of requests hit a cold path and exceed deadline. In practice that looks like intermittent 502s.
[01:10] Elliot Chen: Fencepost? can you rephrase, I'm not sure I follow.
[01:14] Diego Alvarez: Yeah, sorry — fencepost meaning there is a margin mismatch: the cluster will provision 6 GPU slots, the router publishes capacity=6, but the serving runtime reserves one slot per shard for warm cache checks so effectively only 5 are warm. When traffic ramps quickly that last one goes cold and latency spikes. It's subtle and shows up under bursty tenant traffic.
[01:32] Priya Nair: Huh, that checks out. We do these ramp-ups during billing, many tenants concurrently.
[01:38] Maya Brooks: Ok interesting. So mitigation options?
[01:41] Diego Alvarez: Short term: two things — (1) client-side request shaping: add a conservative token-bucket and a jittered backoff so retries don't synchronize, (2) temporary fallback routing: if the preferred model variant is returning 5xx or exceeding deadline, route to a smaller/quantized variant — slightly lower perf but fewer failures.
[02:02] Aisha Rahman: Will fallback change outputs in ways that break product?
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: It can — but we recommend functionally similar variants with minimal delta. We'll provide an evaluation matrix. Also add a header to responses so you can detect fallback in your logs.
[02:15] Samir Patel: We did notice some requests marked as 'backend-fallback' in the logs but we weren't surfacing it properly.
[02:21] Maya Brooks: Right, we'll include a header sample. What about the retry budget — we saw clients hammering retries?
[02:27] Diego Alvarez: We suggest explicit retry budgets per request type. Example: idempotent generation calls get 3 attempts with exponential backoff starting 200ms + jitter; non-idempotent chat flows get only 1 retry. Also honor a global concurrency token so retries don't bypass the shaping.
[02:44] Elliot Chen: Our product team has chat flows that will break with fewer retries. Balancing is hard.
[02:48] Priya Nair: Could Redwood route only billing jobs to Dedicated? we are considering Dedicated but procurement is slow.
[02:54] Maya Brooks: That's on the table — Dedicated removes noisy multi-tenant interference but is a bigger procurement lift. For now the config and routing changes might buy time.
[03:03] Diego Alvarez: On the federation side, we can add per-tenant reservoir sizes and a soft-fence: allow a burst above tenant quota for a short tail window, then throttle back deterministically. That smooths the burst without a hard reject.
[03:18] Samir Patel: We liked the reservoir idea. How do we tune it?
[03:21] Diego Alvarez: Start small: 10% extra for 30s, observe queue depth and SSE/stream tail. We'll share a sample snippet for the reservoir policy.
[03:29] Aisha Rahman: Observability - we couldn't trace the path for the failed requests, there's a gap at service X.
[03:33] Diego Alvarez: Noted. Increase span sampling for the pilot window, and Redwood can add a temporary end-to-end trace capture token that you can attach to failing request IDs.
[03:42] Maya Brooks: We'll also package a 'fencepost-check' harness — a small repro that ramps N tenants and checks for cold-path error rates. Diego, you said you'd produce that?
[03:48] Diego Alvarez: Yep, I'll add a python harness with docker-compose that you can run in a low-traffic window. It will simulate token-bucket bursts and measure 95/99 percentiles and 5xx counts.
[03:58] Elliot Chen: Great. A few security questions from procurement — does fallback routing expose model metadata or logs to other tenants?
[04:06] Maya Brooks: No, fallback is internal to your deployment. If you're on Hosted, data-in-transit is TLS and logs are tenant-scoped. For Private/Dedicated we can provide customer-managed KMS and no cross-tenant exposure. We'll attach SOC2 & network diagrams.
[04:20] Priya Nair: Do you have an example autoscale policy that avoids the fencepost?
[04:24] Diego Alvarez: We'll provide a conservative policy: staggered scaling with warmup probes; basically an add-one-delay per scale event and a minimum slot reservation for KV warm cache. We'll post it to the share.
[04:35] Samir Patel: Any quick config we can flip to reduce immediate risk?
[04:38] Diego Alvarez: Yes: lower client-side concurrency from 10->6 for the billing job path, add a 250ms jittered backoff with cap at 2s, and enable fallback to the quantized-7B for billing route. That should drastically reduce 5xxs while you run the harness.
[04:53] Elliot Chen: Ok we'll try that tonight in staging.
[04:56] Aisha Rahman: One more: how will Redwood surface when the fallback is used so product can flag it?
[04:59] Maya Brooks: We'll add a response header X-Redwood-Fallback: variant=quant7b; and a metric you can query per-tenant. We'll include the PromQL in the sample doc.
[05:09] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Anything else on compliance?
[05:12] Lena Cho: From CSM side, we'll share the compliance kit: SOC2 report, encryption at rest details, and the private deployment checklist. I can email those after the call.
[05:20] Elliot Chen: Perfect. Can we confirm timeline?
[05:23] Maya Brooks: Diego will upload harness + config by 10/08. I'll send the fallback/autoscale snippets by 10/09. NimblePay to run and send logs by 10/12. Follow-up sync 10/13. Procurement check by 10/20.
[05:36] Samir Patel: Quick note: when we ran yesterday we also saw a small uptick in connection resets; might be related to the proxy pool size. We'll include those logs.
[05:44] Diego Alvarez: Thanks, that's helpful, include proxy metrics and we'll correlate connection resets with cold-path incidence.
[05:50] Maya Brooks: Alright let's wrap — any blockers?
[05:52] Elliot Chen: No blockers. We appreciate the tactical plan.
[05:54] Priya Nair: thumbs up.
[05:55] Maya Brooks: Cool, I'll follow up with docs in email and the share link. Thanks everyone.
[05:59] [END]
